text: Continuous investigation of the cubic family y=x^3+ax^2+b, its stationary points, x-axis intercepts and the parameter condition for three real intercepts.

parts.label: a
parts.text: For a=3, find b giving exactly two x-axis intercepts.
parts.scheme: M1: Systematically varies b or otherwise considers the b=0 case. A1: Obtains b=-4 and b=0.

parts.label: b.i
parts.text: For a=3, state b for exactly one x-axis intercept.
parts.scheme: A1: States b<-4 or b>0.

parts.label: b.ii
parts.text: For a=3, state b for exactly three x-axis intercepts.
parts.scheme: A1: States -4<b<0.

parts.label: c.i
parts.text: For a=-3, state b for exactly two x-axis intercepts.
parts.scheme: A1: States b=0 or b=4.

parts.label: c.ii
parts.text: For a=-3, state b for exactly one x-axis intercept.
parts.scheme: A1: States b<0 or b>4.

parts.label: c.iii
parts.text: For a=-3, state b for exactly three x-axis intercepts.
parts.scheme: A1: States 0<b<4.

parts.label: d
parts.text: For three intercepts, locate the zero-gradient points relative to the x-axis.
parts.scheme: A1: States that the two zero-gradient points are on opposite sides of the x-axis.

parts.label: e
parts.text: Show the stationary points P and Q.
parts.scheme: A1: Differentiates to dy/dx=3x^2+2ax. M1: Solves dy/dx=0 to obtain x=0 and x=-2a/3. A1: Identifies P=(0,b) as a stationary point. M1: Substitutes x=-2a/3 into y=x^3+ax^2+b. A1: Obtains Q=(-2a/3,4a^3/27+b) as a stationary point.

parts.label: f.i
parts.text: For a>0,b>0, classify P and Q using the second derivative.
parts.scheme: A1: Finds d^2y/dx^2=6x+2a. R1: Uses d^2y/dx^2=2a>0 at P to classify P as a local minimum. R1: Uses d^2y/dx^2=-2a<0 at Q to classify Q as a local maximum.

parts.label: f.ii
parts.text: For a>0,b>0, locate P and Q relative to the x-axis.
parts.scheme: A1: States P and Q are both above the x-axis.

parts.label: g.i
parts.text: For a<0,b>0, classify and locate P.
parts.scheme: A1: States P is a local maximum and is above the x-axis.

parts.label: g.ii
parts.text: For a<0,b>0, state when Q lies below the x-axis.
parts.scheme: A1: States Q is below the x-axis when 4a^3/27+b<0.

parts.label: h
parts.text: Prove the stated condition gives exactly three x-axis intercepts.
parts.scheme: M1: Attempts to factorize 4a^3b+27b^2<0. A1: Obtains 27b(4a^3/27+b)<0 or b(4a^3+27b)<0. A1: States the two opposite-sign cases for b and 4a^3/27+b. R1: Relates the opposite signs to P and Q lying on opposite sides of the x-axis. R1: Concludes that stationary points on opposite sides of the x-axis give exactly three x-axis intercepts.

solution.outline: For a=3: two intercepts at b=-4,0; one for b<-4 or b>0; three for -4<b<0. For a=-3: two at b=0,4; one for b<0 or b>4; three for 0<b<4. P=(0,b), Q=(-2a/3,4a^3/27+b); 4a^3b+27b^2<0 gives exactly three x-axis intercepts.

text: Continuous investigation of orthogonal and fixed-angle families of curves, including implicit and homogeneous differential equations.

parts.label: a.i
parts.text: Gradient of L in terms of x,y.
parts.scheme: A1: States the gradient of L is y/x.

parts.label: a.ii
parts.text: Gradient of the orthogonal family C.
parts.scheme: A1: Uses negative reciprocal gradients to obtain dy/dx=-x/y.

parts.label: a.iii
parts.text: Solve the differential equation for C.
parts.scheme: M1: Separates variables as y dy=-x dx. A1: Integrates and obtains x^2+y^2=k with a parameter.

parts.label: b
parts.scheme: A1: Sketches y^2=16-8x with approximately correct orientation and position. A1: Sketches y^2=4+4x with approximately correct orientation and position. A1: Labels the x-intercepts 2 and -1.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the intersections of the two parametric curve families.
parts.scheme: A1: Equates 4a^2-4ax and 4b^2+4bx. M1: Factorizes to use (a+b)(a-b)=(a+b)x. R1: Uses a+b>0 to justify division by a+b. A1: Obtains x=a-b. M1: Substitutes x=a-b into either curve equation. A1: Obtains y=plus or minus 2sqrt(ab).

parts.label: d
parts.text: Show the curves meet at right angles at M.
parts.scheme: M1: Attempts implicit differentiation on either curve. A1: Obtains gradients -4a/(2y) and 4b/(2y), or equivalents. M1: Substitutes y=2sqrt(ab) into the gradient expressions. A1: Obtains gradients -sqrt(a/b) and sqrt(b/a), or equivalents. A1: Shows their product is -1 or that they are negative reciprocals.

parts.label: e.i
parts.scheme: A1: Substitutes f=-x/y and tan(alpha)=1 into the fixed-angle formula. A1: Simplifies to g(x,y)=(y-x)/(y+x).

parts.label: e.ii
parts.text: Solve the homogeneous differential equation for G.
parts.scheme: M1: Sets y=vx for the homogeneous differential equation. A1: Uses dy/dx=v+x dv/dx. A1: Substitutes to obtain v+x dv/dx=(v-1)/(v+1). M1: Rearranges to x dv/dx=-(v^2+1)/(v+1). M1: Attempts to separate variables x and v. A1: Separates variables as (v+1)/(v^2+1) dv=-dx/x. A1: Integrates to one-half ln(v^2+1)+arctan(v)=-ln|x|+constant. A1: Substitutes v=y/x. A1: Obtains one-half ln(y^2/x^2+1)+arctan(y/x)+ln|x|=d.

parts.label: f
parts.text: Take the limit as alpha tends to pi/2.
parts.scheme: M1: Rewrites using 1/tan(alpha), or an equivalent sine-cosine form. R1: Uses the limiting values as alpha tends to pi/2 to obtain -1/f(x,y).

solution.outline: C is x^2+y^2=k. The two curve families meet at M(a-b,2sqrt(ab)) and N(a-b,-2sqrt(ab)); at M their gradients have product -1. For alpha=pi/4, g=(y-x)/(y+x), and G is one-half ln(y^2/x^2+1)+arctan(y/x)+ln|x|=d. As alpha tends to pi/2, g tends to -1/f.

text: Continuous investigation of perimeters of regular polygons inscribed in and circumscribed about a unit circle, their limits and bounds for pi.

parts.label: a
parts.scheme: M1: Forms a valid right-triangle or cosine/sine-rule relation for the equilateral triangle. A1: Obtains side length x=sqrt(3). A1: Obtains Pi=3sqrt(3).

parts.label: b
parts.scheme: M1: Uses sin(pi/4)=x/2. A1: Obtains x=sqrt(2). A1: Obtains Pi=4sqrt(2).

parts.label: c
parts.scheme: A1: Recognizes six equilateral triangles and obtains x=1. A1: Obtains Pi=6.

parts.label: d
parts.scheme: M1: Uses sin(pi/n)=x/2 in the right triangle. A1: Obtains x=2sin(pi/n). M1: Uses Pi=n times x.

parts.label: e
parts.text: Limit of the inscribed perimeter using a Maclaurin expansion.
parts.scheme: M1: Uses sin z=z-z^3/3!+z^5/5!-... . A1: Substitutes z=pi/n into 2n sin(pi/n). A1: Simplifies the expansion to 2(pi-pi^3/(6n^2)+...). A1: Obtains lim Pi(n)=2pi. R1: Interprets the limiting polygon as a unit circle with perimeter 2pi.

parts.label: f
parts.scheme: M1: Constructs the 2n right triangles with central angle pi/n. A1: Relates the triangle angle to pi/n. M1: Uses x/2=tan(pi/n). A1: Obtains x=2tan(pi/n).

parts.label: g.i
parts.scheme: R1: Writes P(x)=2tan(pi/x)/(1/x) and recognizes the 0/0 limit form. M1: Attempts L'Hopital's rule. A1: Differentiates numerator and denominator to form the stated sec-squared quotient. A1: Obtains lim P(x)=2pi.

parts.label: g.ii
parts.scheme: A1: States lim Pc(n)=2pi.

parts.label: h
parts.scheme: M1: Uses Pi<2pi<Pc. A1: Obtains n sin(pi/n)<pi<n tan(pi/n).

parts.label: i
parts.text: Least n for the stated accuracy.
parts.scheme: M1: Attempts lower and upper bounds within 0.005 of pi. A1: Finds the least value n=46. A1: Confirms both stated bounds meet the required accuracy at n=46.

solution.outline: Pi(3)=3sqrt(3), Pi(4)=4sqrt(2), Pi(6)=6, Pi(n)=2n sin(pi/n), Pc(n)=2n tan(pi/n); both perimeter limits are 2pi; n sin(pi/n)<pi<n tan(pi/n); the least n is 46.

text: Continuous investigation of the Chebyshev function family f_n(x)=cos(n arccos x), including graphs, stationary points, identities and recurrence.

parts.label: a
parts.scheme: A1: Sketches the correct graph of f1(x). A1: Sketches the correct graph of f3(x).

parts.label: b
parts.text: For odd n, count local extrema.
parts.scheme: M1: Provides graphical or tabular evidence from systematic variation of odd n. A1: Identifies the pattern for odd n extrema. A1: States (n-1)/2 local maximum points. A1: States (n-1)/2 local minimum points.

parts.label: c
parts.scheme: A1: Sketches the correct graph of f2(x). A1: Sketches the correct graph of f4(x).

parts.label: d
parts.text: For even n, count local extrema.
parts.scheme: M1: Provides graphical or tabular evidence from systematic variation of even n. A1: Identifies the pattern for even n extrema. A1: States (n-2)/2 local maximum points. A1: States n/2 local minimum points.

parts.label: e
parts.text: Find the stationary points of fn.
parts.scheme: M1: Uses the chain rule to differentiate fn(x). A1: Obtains f'n(x)=n sin(n arccos x)/sqrt(1-x^2). M1: Sets f'n(x)=0 and obtains n sin(n arccos x)=0. A1: Obtains n arccos(x)=kpi and hence x=cos(kpi/n), 0<k<n.

parts.label: f
parts.scheme: M1: Uses cos(2theta)=2cos^2(theta)-1. A1: Uses cos(arccos x)=x to obtain f2(x)=2x^2-1.

parts.label: g
parts.scheme: A1: Writes f(n+1)(x)=cos(n arccos x+arccos x). M1: Uses cos(A+B)=cos A cos B-sin A sin B to obtain the required identity.

parts.label: h.i

text: For f(x)=mx^2-2mx and y=mx-9 meeting at exactly one point, find m and the equivalent factored and vertex forms, then find where f is negative and increasing.

parts.label: a
parts.scheme: M1: Equates the curve and line to form mx^2-3mx+9=0. M1: Uses the exactly-one-intersection condition discriminant equals zero. A1: Forms discriminant (-3m)^2-4m(9). M1: Solves the resulting equation for m. A1: Obtains candidate values m=0 and m=4. R1: Rejects m=0 because the two graphs would not meet, concluding m=4.

parts.label: b
parts.scheme: A1: Writes f(x)=4x(x-2). A1: Obtains p=0,q=2 or p=2,q=0.

text: For f(x)=6+6cos(x), 0<=x<=4pi, determine the zero-touching points and the enclosed area. A right cone with radius 2 has this area as total surface area; determine l and its volume.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the x-coordinates of A and B.
parts.scheme: M1: Sets 6+6cos(x)=0, or equivalently uses f'(x)=0 for the touching points. A1: Obtains x=pi. A1: Obtains x=3pi.

parts.label: b
parts.scheme: M1: Attempts the definite integral from pi to 3pi of 6+6cos(x). A1: Obtains an antiderivative 6x+6sin(x). A1: Applies the limits pi and 3pi to the antiderivative. M1: Correctly subtracts the two evaluated values. A1: Obtains area=12pi.

parts.label: c
parts.scheme: M1: Attempts the total-surface-area formula including the circular base. A1: Forms pi(2^2)+pi(2)l=12pi. A1: Obtains l=4.

parts.label: d
parts.scheme: M1: Uses the right-triangle relation 2^2+h^2=l^2 to determine the cone height. A1: Obtains h=sqrt(12)=2sqrt(3). M1: Substitutes its radius and height in V=(1/3)pi r^2h. A1: Obtains V=4pi sqrt(12)/3=8pi sqrt(3)/3.

parts.scheme: M1: Uses v'(t)=0, the quadratic vertex, or an equivalent valid turning-point method. A1: Obtains t=2/3 s.

parts.label: a.ii
parts.text: Show the distance then is 88/27 m.
parts.scheme: M1: Attempts to integrate v(t) for displacement. A1: Obtains the antiderivative contribution 4t+2t^2. A1: Obtains the antiderivative contribution -t^3. M1: Substitutes t=2/3 into its displacement expression. A1: Obtains distance 88/27 m.

parts.label: b.i

parts.label: d
parts.text: Find the bearing from A to C.
parts.scheme: A1: Finds angle BAC=48.267…°. M1: Uses the camp bearing and triangle angle to form the required bearing. A1: Bearing=083° (83.3° accepted).

parts.label: e

text: Determine a normal shell-length distribution from a tail probability, use it in binomial expectation/probability calculations, then apply conditional probability.

parts.label: a
parts.scheme: M1: Uses symmetry about the normal-distribution mean. A1: P(24.15<X<25)=0.5−0.1446=0.3554.

parts.label: b.i
parts.scheme: M1: Uses inverse normal to find z=−1.0598. A1: Forms (24.15−25)/σ=−1.0598. A1: σ=0.802.

parts.label: b.ii
parts.scheme: M1: Uses the determined normal distribution to evaluate the upper-tail probability at 26 mm. A1: P(X>26)=0.106.

parts.label: c
parts.scheme: M1: Models Y as binomial with n=10 and p=0.10621… . A1: Forms E(Y)=10×0.10621… . A1: E(Y)=1.06.

parts.label: d
parts.scheme: M1: Evaluates P(Y=3) from the binomial distribution. A1: P(Y=3)=0.0655.

parts.label: e
parts.scheme: M1: Recognizes conditional probability given X<26. A1: Forms 0.3554/(1−0.10621…). A1: Conditional probability=0.398.
